1.why: 〜中 means something is still going on, but this meeting has ended.
1.fix: 会議が始まったので、今、会議中です。
1.fix_en: The meeting has started, so we're in a meeting now.

2.why: 明日中 (by the end of tomorrow) is future, but the verb is past.
2.fix: 明日中に、レポートを出します。
2.fix_en: I'll hand in the report by the end of tomorrow.

3.why: 中 means 'during', so it can't be combined with 後で (after).
3.fix: 食事の後で、薬を飲んでください。
3.fix_en: Please take the medicine after meals.

usage.why_en: 〜中 means 'during / in the middle of'; it can't be used once something has ended, or mixed with 'after' or a past tense like that.

para.s: 次の【駅】で降ります。
para.why: A 駅 is where trains stop.
para.en: I'll get off at the next station.
para.why_en: A 駅 is where trains stop.

options: 駅で飛行機に乗って、北海道へ行った。
駅の前で友達と待ち合わせた。
熱が出たので、駅でみてもらった。
usage.why: Planes leave from airports, ships from ports, and doctors work at hospitals.
opts_en: I got on a plane at the 'station' and went to Hokkaido.
I met up with a friend in front of the station.
I got on a ship at the 'station'.
I had a fever, so I got checked at the 'station'.

0.why: Planes leave from an airport (空港).
0.fix: 空港で飛行機に乗って、北海道へ行った。
0.fix_en: I got on a plane at the airport and went to Hokkaido.

2.why: Ships leave from a port (港).
2.fix: 港で船に乗った。
2.fix_en: I got on a ship at the port.

3.why: You see a doctor at a hospital.
3.fix: 熱が出たので、病院でみてもらった。
3.fix_en: I had a fever, so I got checked at the hospital.

usage.why_en: Planes leave from airports, ships from ports, and doctors work at hospitals.

para.s: 来月から英会話を【始める】つもりだ。
para.why: スタートする means to start.
para.en: I plan to start English conversation from next month.

wrong.2: 続ける means to keep going; it has already started.

para.why_en: スタートする means to start.

options: じゅぎょうが九時に始めます。
映画を最後まで見て、始めました。
九時になったので、会議を始めましょう。
仕事を始めたので、ゆっくり休もう。
usage.why: 始める is transitive (〜を始める); a class itself 始まる, and the end of something is 終わる.
opts_en: I watched the movie to the end and then 'started'.
It's nine o'clock, so let's start the meeting.
I've started work, so let's take it easy.

0.why: The class starts by itself, so use intransitive 始まる.
0.fix: じゅぎょうが九時に始まります。
0.fix_en: Class starts at nine.

1.why: After watching to the end, the movie is over; nothing starts.
1.fix: 映画を最後まで見ました。
1.fix_en: I watched the movie to the end.

3.why: You rest after work ends (終わる), not when it starts.
3.fix: 仕事が終わったので、ゆっくり休もう。
3.fix_en: Work is done, so let's relax.

usage.why_en: 始める is transitive (〜を始める); a class starts by itself (始まる), and when something is over it 終わる.

para.s: 祖母は【病気】で入院している。
para.why: 病気 means being ill (体が悪い).
para.en: My grandmother is in hospital because of illness.

wrong.3: 元気 means healthy, the opposite.

para.why_en: 病気 means being ill (体が悪い).

options: 今日はとても病気で、楽しい。
病気がいいので、外で遊ぼう。
病気が早く治るといいですね。
usage.why: 病気 is illness; being sick is not fun, weather is 天気, and you drink medicine (薬).
opts_en: Today I'm very 'ill', and I'm having fun.
The 'illness' is good, so let's play outside.
I drank 'illness' and went to bed.
I hope your illness gets better soon.

0.why: Being sick doesn't go with having fun; feeling well is 元気.
0.fix: 今日はとても元気で、楽しい。
0.fix_en: I'm feeling great today, and I'm having fun.

1.why: Good weather for playing outside is 天気.
1.fix: 天気がいいので、外で遊ぼう。
1.fix_en: The weather is nice, so let's play outside.

2.why: You drink medicine: 薬.
2.fix: 薬を飲んで、寝た。
2.fix_en: I took some medicine and went to bed.

usage.why_en: 病気 is illness. Being sick isn't fun, nice weather is 天気, and what you drink when sick is medicine (薬).

para.s: 父は毎朝八時に【会社】に行く。
para.why: 勤め先 means one's workplace.
para.en: My father goes to the office at eight every morning.
para.why_en: 勤め先 means one's workplace.

options: 兄は自動車の会社で働いている。
小学生の弟は、毎朝歩いて会社へ行く。
会社で泳いで、体をきたえた。
usage.why: 会社 is a company; hospitals, schools and pools are different places.
opts_en: My older brother works at a car company.
I was hospitalized inside the company.
My little brother, an elementary schooler, walks to the company every morning.
I swam at the company to get in shape.

1.why: You are hospitalized in a hospital (病院).
1.fix: 病院に入院した。
1.fix_en: I was admitted to the hospital.

2.why: An elementary school kid goes to school (学校).
2.fix: 小学生の弟は、毎朝歩いて学校へ行く。
2.fix_en: My little brother, who's in elementary school, walks to school every morning.

3.why: You swim in a pool (プール).
3.fix: プールで泳いで、体をきたえた。
3.fix_en: I swam at the pool to get in shape.

usage.why_en: 会社 is a company; hospitals, schools and pools are different places.

para.s: 姉は来月【けっこんします】。
para.why: For a woman, およめに行く means to get married.
para.en: My older sister is getting married next month.

wrong.0: 引っこす means to move house.
wrong.1: 入院 means to enter hospital.
wrong.2: そつぎょう means to graduate.

para.why_en: For a woman, およめに行く means to get married.

options: 来月、新しい会社とけっこんすることになった。
兄は大学の時の友達とけっこんした。
私はねこと犬をけっこんしている。
試験にけっこんして、大学に入った。
usage.why: けっこん is marriage between people; joining a company, keeping pets and passing exams use other words.
opts_en: Next month I'm going to 'marry' a new company.
My older brother married a friend from his university days.
I am 'married' to a cat and a dog.
I 'married' the exam and got into university.

0.why: You join (入る) a company, not marry it.
0.fix: 来月、新しい会社に入ることになった。
0.fix_en: Next month I'm going to join a new company.

2.why: Keeping pets is かう (飼う).
2.fix: 私はねこと犬をかっている。
2.fix_en: I have a cat and a dog.

3.why: Passing an exam is 合格する.
3.fix: 試験に合格して、大学に入った。
3.fix_en: I passed the exam and got into university.

usage.why_en: けっこん is marriage between people; joining a company, keeping pets and passing exams use other words.

para.s: しおを【少し】入れてください。
para.why: ちょっと means "a little".
para.en: Please add a little salt.

wrong.1: たくさん means a lot, the opposite.
wrong.2: 全部 means all of it.
wrong.3: もっと means more; it compares to before.

para.why_en: ちょっと means 'a little', the same as 少し.

options: 少しの人が集まって、会場に入れなかった。
この料理はとても少しおいしい。
少し休んでから、また仕事を始めよう。
usage.why: 少し means a small amount; a crowd is 大勢, とても少し is wrong, and 少しも needs a negative.
opts_en: 'A few' people gathered, so we couldn't get into the hall.
This dish is very 'a little' tasty.
Let's rest a little, then get back to work.

0.why: If you can't get in, there were many people, not a few.
0.fix: たくさんの人が集まって、会場に入れなかった。
0.fix_en: So many people gathered that we couldn't get into the hall.

1.why: とても (very) and 少し (a little) can't go together.
1.fix: この料理はとてもおいしい。
1.fix_en: This dish is very tasty.

3.why: 少しも must be followed by a negative verb.
3.fix: 少しも分かりませんでした。
3.fix_en: I didn't understand at all.

usage.why_en: 少し means a small amount; a big crowd is たくさん/大勢, とても can't go with 少し, and 少しも needs a negative.

para.s: お茶でも【飲みませんか】。
para.why: お茶でもいかがですか is a polite way to offer a drink.
para.en: Won't you have some tea?
para.why_en: お茶でもいかがですか is a polite way to offer a drink.

options: パンを飲んで、学校へ行った。
寒いので、熱いおふろを飲んだ。
子供が友達とボールを飲んで遊んでいる。
かぜをひいたので、薬を飲んで寝た。
usage.why: 飲む is for drinks and medicine; bread is eaten, baths are entered, balls are played with.
opts_en: I 'drank' bread and went to school.
It was cold, so I 'drank' a hot bath.
The child is 'drinking' a ball and playing with friends.
I caught a cold, so I took medicine and went to bed.

0.why: Bread is eaten: 食べる.
0.fix: パンを食べて、学校へ行った。
0.fix_en: I ate some bread and went to school.

1.why: You get into a bath: おふろに入る.
1.fix: 寒いので、熱いおふろに入った。
1.fix_en: It was cold, so I took a hot bath.

2.why: You play with a ball: ボールで遊ぶ.
2.fix: 子供が友達とボールで遊んでいる。
2.fix_en: The child is playing ball with friends.

usage.why_en: 飲む is for drinks and medicine. Bread is eaten (食べる), you get into a bath (入る), and you play with a ball.

para.s: この【水】は飲めません。
para.why: ウォーター is a loanword meaning water.
para.en: You can't drink this water.
para.why_en: ウォーター is a loanword meaning water.

options: あついので、冷たい水が飲みたい。
冷たい水でやけどをした。
usage.why: Heaters are turned on, burns come from hot water, and books are counted in さつ.
opts_en: It's hot, so I want to drink cold water.
It's cold, so I turned on the water.
I got burned by cold water.

1.why: When it's cold you turn on a heater (ストーブ).
1.fix: 寒いので、ストーブをつけた。
1.fix_en: It was cold, so I turned on the heater.

2.why: Burns come from hot water (お湯), not cold water.
2.fix: 熱いお湯でやけどをした。
2.fix_en: I burned myself with hot water.

3.why: さつ counts books, not water.
3.fix: 本が三さつある。
3.fix_en: There are three books.

usage.why_en: When it's cold you turn on a heater, burns come from hot water (お湯), and さつ counts books.

para.s: 新しいパソコンが【欲しい】。
para.why: Wanting a new PC means you want to buy one.
para.en: I want a new computer.

wrong.0: 売りたい means want to sell, the opposite.
wrong.1: 使いにくい means hard to use.

para.why_en: Wanting a new PC means you want to buy one.

options: 私は来年、日本へ欲しいです。
たんじょう日に新しい時計が欲しい。
私はもう一度その映画を見て欲しい。
部屋がきれいで、とても欲しい。
usage.why: 欲しい is for things you want; for your own actions use 〜たい (行きたい, 見たい).
opts_en: I want a new watch for my birthday.
I 'want someone else' to see that movie once more (but I mean myself).
The room is clean, so I 'want' it very much.

0.why: For your own action (going), use 〜たい.
0.fix: 私は来年、日本へ行きたいです。
0.fix_en: I want to go to Japan next year.

2.why: 〜て欲しい means wanting someone else to do it; for yourself use 〜たい.
2.fix: 私はもう一度その映画を見たい。
2.fix_en: I want to see that movie once more.

3.why: This describes how the room feels, not something you want to get.
3.fix: 部屋がきれいで、とても気持ちがいい。
3.fix_en: The room is clean and feels very nice.

usage.why_en: 欲しい is for things you want; for your own actions use 〜たい (行きたい, 見たい).

para.s: 飛行機は九時に【出発】する。
para.why: 出発する means to leave / depart (出る).
para.en: The plane departs at nine.

wrong.1: 着く means arrive, the opposite.

para.why_en: 出発する means to leave or depart (出る).

options: 電車が駅に出発しました。
テレビの番組が出発した。
明日の朝六時にホテルを出発します。
新しい店が駅前に出発した。
usage.why: 出発 is departure; arriving is 到着, programs 始まる, and a new shop できる.
opts_en: The train 'departed' at the station (meant: arrived).
We'll leave the hotel at six tomorrow morning.
A new shop 'departed' in front of the station.

0.why: 駅に (at/to the station) points to arriving, not leaving.
0.fix: 電車が駅に着きました。
0.fix_en: The train arrived at the station.

1.why: A TV program begins (始まる); it doesn't depart.
1.fix: テレビの番組が始まった。
1.fix_en: The TV program started.

3.why: A new shop opens (できる); it doesn't depart.
3.fix: 新しい店が駅前にできた。
3.fix_en: A new shop opened in front of the station.

usage.why_en: 出発 means departure; arriving is 到着/着く, a program 始まる, and a new shop できる.

para.s: 空から雪が【降って】きた。
para.why: Snow falling from the sky is "coming down" (落ちてくる).
para.en: Snow started falling from the sky.

wrong.0: 上がる means to go up, the opposite.

para.why_en: Snow falling from the sky is coming down, i.e. 落ちてくる.

options: 強い風が降って、木がたおれた。
次の駅で電車を降るときは、気をつけてください。
熱が降って、元気になった。
朝から雪が降っていて、外は真っ白だ。
usage.why: 降る is for rain and snow; wind 吹く, getting off a train is 降りる, and fevers 下がる.
opts_en: A strong wind 'fell', and a tree fell over.
Please be careful when you 'fall' the train at the next station.
My fever 'fell', and I got better.
It's been snowing since morning, and everything outside is white.

0.why: Wind blows: 吹く.
0.fix: 強い風が吹いて、木がたおれた。
0.fix_en: A strong wind blew, and a tree fell over.

1.why: Getting off a train is 降りる, a different verb.
1.fix: 次の駅で電車を降りるときは、気をつけてください。
1.fix_en: Please be careful when you get off the train at the next station.

2.why: A fever goes down: 下がる.
2.fix: 熱が下がって、元気になった。
2.fix_en: My fever went down, and I got better.

usage.why_en: 降る is for rain and snow falling. Wind blows (吹く), getting off a train is 降りる, and a fever goes down (下がる).

para.s: うちの【息子】は今年大学生になった。
para.why: 息子 is one's son (male child).
para.en: Our son became a university student this year.
para.why_en: 息子 is one's son (male child).

options: 息子は来年、小学校に入ります。
姉には息子が二人いて、二人とも女の子です。
私の息子は私より三十歳上です。
母の息子は私の姉です。
usage.why: A son is male and younger than his parent.
opts_en: My son starts elementary school next year.
My older sister has two sons, and both are girls.
My son is thirty years older than me.
My mother's son is my older sister.

1.why: A son is a boy, so he can't be a girl; say 子ども.
1.fix: 姉には子どもが二人いて、二人とも女の子です。
1.fix_en: My older sister has two children, and both are girls.

2.why: A son is younger than his parent; someone thirty years older is your father.
2.fix: 私の父は私より三十歳上です。
2.fix_en: My father is thirty years older than me.

3.why: A son is male, so he can't be a sister.
3.fix: 母の息子は私の兄です。
3.fix_en: My mother's son is my older brother.

usage.why_en: A son (息子) is male and younger than his parent.

para.s: その【言葉】の意味を辞書で調べた。
para.why: 単語 means "word".
para.en: I looked up the meaning of that word in a dictionary.
para.why_en: 単語 means 'word'.

options: 先生の言葉を聞いて、元気が出た。
言葉が高くて、買えなかった。
usage.why: 言葉 are words that are said or heard, not physical objects.
opts_en: Hearing my teacher's words cheered me up.
The 'words' were expensive, so I couldn't buy it.

0.why: You take photos with a camera.
0.fix: カメラで写真をとった。
0.fix_en: I took a photo with a camera.

2.why: Words aren't objects you can sit on; use いす.
2.fix: いすの上に座った。
2.fix_en: I sat on the chair.

3.why: What's expensive is the price (値段).
3.fix: 値段が高くて、買えなかった。
3.fix_en: The price was high, so I couldn't buy it.

usage.why_en: 言葉 are words that are said or heard, not physical objects.

para.s: その店はコーヒーの値段を【上げた】。
para.why: Raising a price means making it higher.
para.en: That shop raised the price of coffee.

wrong.1: 安くした means made cheaper, the opposite.
wrong.2: 変えなかった means didn't change it.
wrong.3: 下げた means lowered, the opposite.

para.why_en: Raising a price means making it higher (高くした).

options: かいだんを上げて、二かいへ行った。
本を読むときは、電気を上げてください。
分かった人は手を上げてください。
雨が上げたら、出かけよう。
usage.why: 上げる is transitive; going upstairs and rain stopping use 上がる, and lights are つける.
opts_en: I 'raised' the stairs and went to the second floor.
When you read, please 'raise' the light.
If you understand, please raise your hand.
When the rain 'raises (something)', let's go out.

0.why: Going up stairs is intransitive 上がる.
0.fix: かいだんを上がって、二かいへ行った。
0.fix_en: I went up the stairs to the second floor.

1.why: Turning on a light is つける.
1.fix: 本を読むときは、電気をつけてください。
1.fix_en: Please turn on the light when you read.

3.why: Rain stopping is 雨が上がる (intransitive).
3.fix: 雨が上がったら、出かけよう。
3.fix_en: Let's go out when the rain stops.

usage.why_en: 上げる is transitive (raise something); going upstairs and rain stopping use 上がる, and lights use つける.

para.s: 山の上から見た景色は【美しかった】。
para.why: きれい means beautiful.
para.en: The view from the mountaintop was beautiful.

wrong.0: きたない means dirty, the opposite.

para.why_en: きれい means beautiful.

options: 部屋が美しいので、そうじした。
このラーメンはとても美しい味がする。
道が美しくて、車が通れない。
秋になると、山が赤やきいろになって美しい。
usage.why: 美しい is for beautiful sights; taste is おいしい, and a narrow road is せまい.
opts_en: The room was beautiful, so I cleaned it.
This ramen has a very 'beautiful' taste.
The road is so 'beautiful' that cars can't get through.
In autumn the mountains turn red and yellow and are beautiful.

0.why: You clean a room because it's dirty: きたない.
0.fix: 部屋がきたないので、そうじした。
0.fix_en: The room was dirty, so I cleaned it.

1.why: Taste is described with おいしい.
1.fix: このラーメンはとてもおいしい。
1.fix_en: This ramen is really tasty.

2.why: A road cars can't pass is narrow: せまい.
2.fix: 道がせまくて、車が通れない。
2.fix_en: The road is so narrow that cars can't get through.

usage.why_en: 美しい is for beautiful sights. Good taste is おいしい, and a road too small for cars is せまい.

para.s: 私が生まれた【町】はとても小さい。
para.why: 市 (city) is closest to 町 (town).
para.en: The town I was born in is very small.

wrong.0: 国 is a country, far too big.

para.why_en: 市 (city) is the closest to 町 (town).

options: この町には古いおてらがたくさんある。
このかばんの町にさいふがある。
usage.why: 町 is a town; inside a bag is 中, a job is 仕事, and lessons are about subjects.
opts_en: This town has many old temples.
My wallet is in the 'town' of this bag.

1.why: Inside a bag is 中.
1.fix: このかばんの中にさいふがある。
1.fix_en: My wallet is in this bag.

2.why: A job is 仕事.
2.fix: 父の仕事は医者です。
2.fix_en: My father is a doctor.

3.why: You take lessons in a skill or subject, like piano, not a town.
3.fix: 毎週、ピアノを習っている。
3.fix_en: I take piano lessons every week.

usage.why_en: 町 is a town; inside a bag is 中, a job is 仕事, and lessons are for a skill or subject.

para.s: 夏休みに国へ【帰る】つもりです。
para.why: 戻る means to return.
para.en: I plan to go back to my country for summer vacation.

wrong.0: 出かける means go out.

para.why_en: 戻る means to return.

options: 初めて日本へ帰ったのは、三年前です。
仕事が終わったら、まっすぐ家に帰る。
借りた本を図書館に帰った。
毎朝七時に会社へ帰ります。
usage.why: 帰る is returning to where you belong; a first visit is 来る/行く, books are 返す, going to work is 行く.
opts_en: The first time I 'returned' to Japan was three years ago.
When work is over, I go straight home.
I 'went home' the borrowed book to the library.
Every morning at seven I 'go home' to the office.

0.why: A first visit isn't a return; use 来る.
0.fix: 初めて日本へ来たのは、三年前です。
0.fix_en: The first time I came to Japan was three years ago.

2.why: Returning a thing is 返す; 帰る is for people going back.
2.fix: 借りた本を図書館に返した。
2.fix_en: I returned the borrowed book to the library.

3.why: Going to work is 行く; you 帰る home.
3.fix: 毎朝七時に会社へ行きます。
3.fix_en: Every morning I go to the office at seven.

usage.why_en: 帰る is going back to where you belong; a first visit is 来る/行く, things are 返す, and going to work is 行く.

para.s: 育てていた花が【死んで】しまった。
para.why: For plants, dying is かれる (to wither).
para.en: The flowers I was growing died.

wrong.1: さく means bloomed, the opposite.
wrong.3: 生まれる means were born.

para.why_en: For plants, dying is かれる (to wither).

options: 電気が死んだので、部屋が暗くなった。
雨が死んだので、出かけた。
かっていた金魚が死んで、子供が悲しんでいる。
試合で死んで、くやしかった。
usage.why: 死ぬ is for living things; lights 消える, rain やむ, and games are 負ける.
opts_en: The light 'died' (passed away), so the room got dark.
The rain 'died', so I went out.
Our pet goldfish died, and my child is sad.
I 'died' in the match and was frustrated.

0.why: Unlike English, a light can't 'die' in Japanese; it goes out (消える).
0.fix: 電気が消えたので、部屋が暗くなった。
0.fix_en: The light went out, so the room got dark.

1.why: Rain stops (やむ).
1.fix: 雨がやんだので、出かけた。
1.fix_en: The rain stopped, so I went out.

3.why: Losing a match is 負ける.
3.fix: 試合で負けて、くやしかった。
3.fix_en: I lost the match and was frustrated.

usage.why_en: 死ぬ is only for living things; lights go out (消える), rain stops (やむ), and you lose (負ける) a match.

para.s: 会議は五時に【終わった】。
para.why: すむ means to be finished.
para.en: The meeting ended at five.

wrong.0: 始まる means started, the opposite.
wrong.2: 止まる means stopped (as a motion).

para.why_en: すむ means to be finished.

options: 宿題を早く終わって、遊びに行った。
新しい店が終わって、毎日にぎやかだ。
じゅぎょうが終わったら、図書館へ行こう。
usage.why: 終わる is intransitive (〜が終わる); with を use 終える, trains 着く, new shops できる.
opts_en: I 'ended' my homework early and went out to play.
A new shop 'ended', and it's lively every day.
When class is over, let's go to the library.

0.why: With を you need the transitive 終える.
0.fix: 宿題を早く終えて、遊びに行った。
0.fix_en: I finished my homework early and went out to play.

1.why: A train arriving at a station is 着く.
1.fix: 電車が駅に着いた。
1.fix_en: The train arrived at the station.

2.why: A new shop opening is できる.
2.fix: 新しい店ができて、毎日にぎやかだ。
2.fix_en: A new shop opened, and it's lively every day.

usage.why_en: 終わる is intransitive (〜が終わる). With を use 終える; a train arrives (着く), and a new shop opens (できる).

para.s: 熱があるので、【医者】にみてもらった。
para.why: 医師 is a formal word for doctor.
para.en: I had a fever, so I saw a doctor.

wrong.0: かんごし is a nurse.
wrong.1: 店員 is a shop clerk.
wrong.3: せんぱい is a senior.

para.why_en: 医師 is a formal word for doctor.

options: 医者に、たばこはやめたほうがいいと言われた。
車が動かないので、医者に直してもらった。
医者に髪を切ってもらった。
usage.why: 医者 is a person, not a place (病院で); cars and hair are handled by other people.
opts_en: The doctor told me I should quit smoking.
I got medicine 'at the doctor' (as a place).
My car wouldn't run, so I had a doctor fix it.
I had a doctor cut my hair.

1.why: 医者 is a person; for the place (で) say 病院.
1.fix: 病院で薬をもらった。
1.fix_en: I got medicine at the hospital.

2.why: Cars are fixed at a car shop, not by a doctor.
2.fix: 車が動かないので、車屋さんに直してもらった。
2.fix_en: My car wouldn't run, so I had the car shop fix it.

3.why: Hair is cut by a barber (とこやさん).
3.fix: とこやさんに髪を切ってもらった。
3.fix_en: I had the barber cut my hair.

usage.why_en: 医者 is a person, not a place (use 病院で), and cars and hair are handled by other people.

para.s: 駅の前に車を【止めない】でください。
para.why: 車を止める means to park (ちゅうしゃする).
para.en: Please don't stop your car in front of the station.

wrong.0: 運転しない means don't drive; the issue is leaving the car there.
wrong.1: 洗わない means don't wash it.
wrong.2: 売らない means don't sell it.

para.why_en: 車を止める here means to park (ちゅうしゃする).

options: バスが駅の前に止めた。
雨が止めたら、出かけよう。
時計が止めて、時間が分からない。
usage.why: 止める is transitive (〜を止める); a bus or clock 止まる, and rain やむ.
opts_en: The bus 'stopped' (transitive) in front of the station.
I stopped the car at a red light.
When the rain 'stops' (transitive), let's go out.
The clock 'stopped' (transitive), so I don't know the time.

0.why: The bus stops by itself, so use 止まる.
0.fix: バスが駅の前に止まった。
0.fix_en: The bus stopped in front of the station.

2.why: Rain stopping is やむ.
2.fix: 雨がやんだら、出かけよう。
2.fix_en: When the rain stops, let's go out.

3.why: The clock stops by itself, so use 止まる.
3.fix: 時計が止まって、時間が分からない。
3.fix_en: My clock stopped, so I don't know the time.

usage.why_en: 止める is transitive (〜を止める, to stop something); a bus or a clock 止まる by itself, and rain やむ.

para.s: 駅からバスに【乗って】ください。
para.why: 乗車する is the formal word for getting on a vehicle.
para.en: Please get on the bus from the station.

wrong.1: 降りる means to get off, the opposite.
wrong.3: 乗りかえる means to change to another vehicle.

para.why_en: 乗車する is the formal word for getting on a vehicle.

options: かいだんに乗って、二かいへ行った。
新しい会社に乗って、もう三年になる。
毎朝、七時の電車に乗る。
疲れたので、いすに乗って休んだ。
usage.why: 乗る is for vehicles; stairs are 上がる, a company is 入る, and chairs are 座る.
opts_en: I 'rode' the stairs to the second floor.
It's been three years since I 'rode' the new company.
Every morning I take the 7:00 train.
I was tired, so I 'rode' a chair and rested.

0.why: Going up stairs is 上がる.
0.fix: かいだんを上がって、二かいへ行った。
0.fix_en: I went up the stairs to the second floor.

1.why: Joining a company is 入る.
1.fix: 新しい会社に入って、もう三年になる。
1.fix_en: It's been three years since I joined the new company.

3.why: You sit (座る) on a chair.
3.fix: 疲れたので、いすに座って休んだ。
3.fix_en: I was tired, so I sat on a chair and rested.

usage.why_en: 乗る is for getting on vehicles; stairs are 上がる, joining a company is 入る, and chairs are 座る.

para.s: 電車にかさを【忘れて】しまった。
para.why: 忘れる here means to leave something behind.
para.en: I left my umbrella on the train.

wrong.0: 持ってくる means brought it, the opposite.

para.why_en: 忘れる here means to leave something behind (置いてくる).

options: 古い服を忘れて、新しいのを買った。
かぎを忘れて、ドアを開けた。
試合に忘れて、くやしかった。
宿題を家に忘れてきた。
usage.why: 忘れる is to forget; throwing away is すてる, a key is 使う to open a door, and games are 負ける.
opts_en: I 'forgot' my old clothes and bought new ones.
I 'forgot' the key and opened the door.
I 'forgot' the match and was frustrated.
I left my homework at home.

0.why: Getting rid of old clothes is すてる.
0.fix: 古い服をすてて、新しいのを買った。
0.fix_en: I threw away my old clothes and bought new ones.

1.why: You use a key to open a door: 使う.
1.fix: かぎを使って、ドアを開けた。
1.fix_en: I used the key to open the door.

2.why: Losing a match is 負ける.
2.fix: 試合に負けて、くやしかった。
2.fix_en: I lost the match and was frustrated.

usage.why_en: 忘れる is to forget or leave something behind. Getting rid of things is すてる, a key is used (使う) to open a door, and losing a game is 負ける.

para.s: 兄はまだ【学生】です。
para.why: Here 学生 means a university student.
para.en: My older brother is still a student.

wrong.0: 社会人 is a working adult, the opposite.
wrong.3: 会社員 is an office worker.

para.why_en: Here 学生 means a university student.

options: この店は安いので、学生に人気がある。
学生になったので、会社で働き始めた。
この学生はとてもおいしい。
usage.why: 学生 is a student; starting work means becoming a 社会人.
opts_en: This shop is cheap, so it's popular with students.
I became a student, so I started working at a company.

1.why: Starting work means you've finished being a student, e.g. graduated.
1.fix: 大学を卒業したので、会社で働き始めた。
1.fix_en: I graduated from university, so I started working at a company.

2.why: People aren't 'delicious'; this fits food, like a cake.
2.fix: このケーキはとてもおいしい。
2.fix_en: This cake is very tasty.

3.why: 本 counts long thin things like pens, not people.
3.fix: ペンが三本ある。
3.fix_en: There are three pens.

usage.why_en: 学生 is a student; starting work means becoming a working adult (社会人).

para.s: この町は外国人が【多い】。
para.why: 多い means there are many (たくさんいる).
para.en: This town has a lot of foreigners.

wrong.0: 少ない means few, the opposite.

para.why_en: 多い means there are many (たくさんいる).

options: この部屋は多くて、気持ちがいい。
このかばんはとても多い。
多い人が駅に集まった。
usage.why: 多い means many in number; a room is 広い, a bag 重い, and before a noun it becomes 多くの.
opts_en: This room is 'many' and feels nice.
There was a lot of rain this year.

0.why: A big room is 広い; 多い is about number.
0.fix: この部屋は広くて、気持ちがいい。
0.fix_en: This room is spacious and feels nice.

2.why: A bag is heavy (重い), not many.
2.fix: このかばんはとても重い。
2.fix_en: This bag is very heavy.

3.why: Before a noun, 多い becomes 多くの (or use たくさんの).
3.fix: 多くの人が駅に集まった。
3.fix_en: Many people gathered at the station.

usage.why_en: 多い means many in number; a room is 広い, a bag 重い, and before a noun it becomes 多くの.

para.s: 子供たちが校庭を【走って】いる。
para.why: かける (駆ける) means to run.
para.en: The children are running in the schoolyard.
para.why_en: かける (駆ける) means to run.

options: 雨が走って、かさをさした。
遅れそうだったので、駅まで走った。
usage.why: 走る is running on legs; fish swim, rain falls and birds fly.
opts_en: Fish are running in the river.
The rain 'ran', so I opened my umbrella.
I was going to be late, so I ran to the station.
Birds are running in the sky.

0.why: Fish swim (泳ぐ).
0.fix: 魚が川を泳いでいる。
0.fix_en: Fish are swimming in the river.

1.why: Rain falls (降る).
1.fix: 雨が降ってきたので、かさをさした。
1.fix_en: It started raining, so I opened my umbrella.

3.why: Birds in the sky fly (飛ぶ).
3.fix: 鳥が空を飛んでいる。
3.fix_en: Birds are flying in the sky.

usage.why_en: 走る is running on legs; fish swim, rain falls, and birds fly.

para.s: 夏休みに【国】へ帰ります。
para.why: Going back to one's 国 means going back to one's homeland (ふるさと).
para.en: I'm going back to my home country for summer vacation.
para.why_en: Going back to one's 国 means going back to one's homeland (ふるさと).

options: この国はかばんの中に入っている。
世界にはたくさんの国がある。
usage.why: 国 is a country; it cannot fit in a bag, grow like a tree, or be read.
opts_en: There are many countries in the world.

0.why: A country can't fit in a bag.
0.fix: この本はかばんの中に入っている。
0.fix_en: This book is in the bag.

1.why: Something counted with 本 in a garden is a tree.
1.fix: 庭に木が一本ある。
1.fix_en: There's a tree in the garden.

2.why: Things you read, counted with さつ, are books.
2.fix: 本を三さつ読んだ。
2.fix_en: I read three books.

usage.why_en: 国 is a country; it can't fit in a bag, grow in a garden, or be read.

para.s: このテストは【あまり】難しくなかった。
para.why: あまり〜ない means "not very", like そんなに〜ない.
para.en: This test wasn't very difficult.

wrong.0: とても doesn't mean 'not very' with a negative.
wrong.1: 少しも〜ない means 'not at all', too strong.
wrong.3: ぜんぜん〜ない means 'not at all', too strong.

para.why_en: あまり〜ない means 'not very', like そんなに〜ない.

options: 今日はあまり寒くない。
この料理はあまりおいしいです。
あまり雨が降っている。
兄はあまり背が高いです。
usage.why: あまり meaning "not very" needs a negative ending.
opts_en: This dish is 'not very' tasty — but the verb is positive.
It's 'not much' raining — but the verb is positive.
My older brother is 'not very' tall — but the verb is positive.

1.why: あまり meaning 'not very' needs a negative ending.
1.fix: この料理はあまりおいしくないです。
1.fix_en: This dish isn't very tasty.

2.why: あまり needs a negative ending like 〜ていない.
2.fix: あまり雨が降っていない。
2.fix_en: It isn't raining much.

3.why: あまり needs a negative ending like 〜くない.
3.fix: 兄はあまり背が高くないです。
3.fix_en: My older brother isn't very tall.

usage.why_en: When あまり means 'not very / not much', the sentence must end in a negative.

para.s: 来月、日本語の試験を【受ける】。
para.why: 受験する means to take an exam.
para.en: Next month I'll take a Japanese exam.

wrong.0: 作る means to make the exam.
wrong.2: 合格する means to pass, not just take it.

para.why_en: 受験する means to take an exam.

options: 試験を受けて、生徒に配った。
来年、大学の入学試験を受けるつもりだ。
毎朝、シャワーを受けてから出かける。
試合に受けて、うれしかった。
usage.why: 受ける is for exams; a teacher makes a test (作る), showers are あびる, and games are 勝つ.
opts_en: I 'took' the exam and handed it out to the students.
I plan to take the university entrance exam next year.
Every morning I 'receive' a shower before going out.
I 'received' the match and was happy.

0.why: A teacher who hands out a test made it (作る).
0.fix: 試験を作って、生徒に配った。
0.fix_en: I made the test and handed it out to the students.

2.why: Taking a shower is シャワーをあびる.
2.fix: 毎朝、シャワーをあびてから出かける。
2.fix_en: Every morning I take a shower before going out.

3.why: Winning a match is 勝つ.
3.fix: 試合に勝って、うれしかった。
3.fix_en: I won the match and was happy.

usage.why_en: 受ける is used for taking exams; a teacher makes (作る) a test, showers are あびる, and matches are 勝つ.

para.s: 明日、英語の【試験】がある。
para.why: テスト is the same as 試験.
para.en: There's an English exam tomorrow.

wrong.2: じゅぎょう is a class.

para.why_en: テスト is the same as 試験.

options: 試験をかけて、友達と話した。
試験でお金を下ろした。
試験の前の日は、早く寝たほうがいい。
昨日の試験はとてもおいしかった。
usage.why: 試験 is an exam; phones are かける, money comes from a bank, and food is おいしい.
opts_en: I 'called' the exam and talked with my friend.
I withdrew money at the exam.
The day before an exam, you should go to bed early.

0.why: Making a call is 電話をかける.
0.fix: 電話をかけて、友達と話した。
0.fix_en: I made a phone call and talked with my friend.

1.why: You withdraw money at a bank.
1.fix: 銀行でお金を下ろした。
1.fix_en: I withdrew money at the bank.

3.why: Only food can be tasty.
3.fix: 昨日の料理はとてもおいしかった。
3.fix_en: Yesterday's food was very tasty.

usage.why_en: 試験 is an exam; phone calls are かける, money comes out of a bank, and food is おいしい.

para.s: この問題は【難しい】。
para.why: 難しい means "not easy".
para.en: This problem is difficult.

wrong.0: かんたん means easy, the opposite.

para.why_en: 難しい means 'not easy'.

options: このにもつは難しくて、持てない。
店の人が難しくて、うれしかった。
問題が難しいので、すぐに答えられた。
この漢字は難しくて、読めない。
usage.why: 難しい means hard to do or understand; heavy is 重い, and hard questions cannot be answered quickly.
opts_en: This luggage is so 'difficult' I can't carry it.
The shop clerk was 'difficult', and I was happy.
The question was difficult, so I could answer it right away.
This kanji is difficult, and I can't read it.

0.why: Luggage you can't carry is heavy: 重い.
0.fix: このにもつは重くて、持てない。
0.fix_en: This luggage is so heavy I can't carry it.

1.why: A clerk who made you happy was kind: 親切.
1.fix: 店の人が親切で、うれしかった。
1.fix_en: The shop clerk was kind, and I was happy.

2.why: If you answered right away, the question was easy: やさしい.
2.fix: 問題がやさしいので、すぐに答えられた。
2.fix_en: The question was easy, so I could answer it right away.

usage.why_en: 難しい means hard to do or understand. Too heavy to carry is 重い, and a hard question can't be answered right away.

para.s: 駅員さんが【親切に】道を教えてくれた。
para.why: 親切に means kindly (やさしく).
para.en: The station worker kindly told me the way.

wrong.0: こわく means in a scary way.

para.why_en: 親切に means kindly (やさしく).

options: となりの人はいつも親切にしてくれる。
このラーメンは親切だ。
今日は天気が親切で、気持ちがいい。
店員がとても親切で、気分が悪かった。
usage.why: 親切 describes kind people; food and weather are not 親切, and kindness does not make you feel bad.
opts_en: The person next door is always kind to me.
The weather is kind today, and I feel good.
The clerk was very kind, so I felt bad.

1.why: Food isn't kind; 親切 describes people.
1.fix: このラーメンはおいしい。
1.fix_en: This ramen is tasty.

2.why: Nice weather is いい, not 親切.
2.fix: 今日は天気がよくて、気持ちがいい。
2.fix_en: The weather is nice today, and it feels good.

3.why: Kindness would make you feel good, not bad.
3.fix: 店員がとても親切で、気分がよかった。
3.fix_en: The clerk was very kind, so I felt good.

usage.why_en: 親切 describes kind people; food and weather aren't 親切, and kindness doesn't make you feel bad.

para.s: その店には【若い】客が多い。
para.why: 若い means young, not old.
para.en: That shop has many young customers.

wrong.0: 年をとった means old, the opposite.

para.why_en: 若い means young, i.e. not old.

options: この家は去年建てたので、まだ若い。
父は若いころ、外国で働いていた。
このパンは若いので、おいしい。
先月買ったばかりの若い車に乗っている。
usage.why: 若い is for people and living things; new objects are 新しい.
opts_en: This house was built last year, so it's still 'young'.
When my father was young, he worked abroad.
This bread is 'young', so it's tasty.
I drive a 'young' car I bought just last month.

0.why: Things are new (新しい), not young.
0.fix: この家は去年建てたので、まだ新しい。
0.fix_en: This house was built last year, so it's still new.

2.why: Bread is new/fresh, not young.
2.fix: このパンは新しいので、おいしい。
2.fix_en: This bread is fresh, so it's tasty.

3.why: A car is new (新しい), not young.
3.fix: 先月買ったばかりの新しい車に乗っている。
3.fix_en: I drive a new car I bought just last month.

usage.why_en: 若い is for people and living things; new objects are 新しい.

para.s: 【友達】と映画を見に行った。
para.why: 友人 is a slightly formal word for friend.
para.en: I went to see a movie with a friend.

wrong.3: 店員 is a shop clerk.

para.why_en: 友人 is a slightly formal word for friend.

options: 友達とカフェで二時間話した。
usage.why: 友達 is a person; pens and cameras are used to write and take photos.
opts_en: I wrote a letter with a 'friend' (as a tool).
I talked with my friend at a café for two hours.
I took a photo with a 'friend' (as a tool).

0.why: 本 and ある are for objects like pens; people use 人 and いる.
0.fix: ペンが三本ある。
0.fix_en: There are three pens.

1.why: で here marks the tool you write with, like a pen.
1.fix: ペンで手紙を書いた。
1.fix_en: I wrote a letter with a pen.

3.why: で here marks the tool, like a camera (with a person, use と).
3.fix: カメラで写真をとった。
3.fix_en: I took a photo with a camera.

usage.why_en: 友達 is a person; で marks a tool here, and you write with a pen and take photos with a camera.

para.s: 試験に【失敗した】。
para.why: 試験に失敗する means to fail (落ちる) an exam.
para.en: I failed the exam.

wrong.0: 合格 means passed, the opposite.
wrong.3: 受ける means took it, not the result.

para.why_en: 試験に失敗する means to fail (落ちる) an exam.

options: 道に失敗して、遅くなった。
駅でさいふを失敗した。
失敗して、みんなにほめられた。
料理に失敗して、ケーキが黒くなった。
usage.why: 失敗 is failing at a task; getting lost is 迷う, losing a wallet is なくす, and failure is not praised.
opts_en: I 'failed' the road and was late.
I 'failed' my wallet at the station.
I failed, and everyone praised me.
My cooking went wrong, and the cake turned black.

0.why: Getting lost is 道に迷う.
0.fix: 道に迷って、遅くなった。
0.fix_en: I got lost and was late.

1.why: Losing a wallet is なくす.
1.fix: 駅でさいふをなくした。
1.fix_en: I lost my wallet at the station.

2.why: People praise success, not failure: 成功.
2.fix: 成功して、みんなにほめられた。
2.fix_en: I succeeded, and everyone praised me.

usage.why_en: 失敗 is failing at a task. Getting lost is 道に迷う, losing a wallet is なくす, and failing doesn't get you praise.

para.s: たなの【高い】ところにある箱を取ってください。
para.why: A high place on a shelf is the upper part (上の方).
para.en: Please get the box in the high place on the shelf.

wrong.0: 下の方 means the lower part, the opposite.
wrong.1: 前の方 means the front part.
wrong.3: おくの方 means the back part.

para.why_en: A high place on a shelf is the upper part (上の方).

options: このレストランはおいしいけど、少し高い。
このスープは高くて飲めない。
usage.why: Hot soup is 熱い, older is 年が上, and many people is 多い.
opts_en: This restaurant is good, but a bit expensive.
This soup is so 'high' I can't drink it.

1.why: Soup too hot to drink is 熱い.
1.fix: このスープは熱くて飲めない。
1.fix_en: This soup is too hot to drink.

2.why: For being older, say 年が上.
2.fix: 父は母より年が上だ。
2.fix_en: My father is older than my mother.

3.why: For a lot of people, say 多い.
3.fix: 電車の中は人が多い。
3.fix_en: There are a lot of people on the train.

usage.why_en: Hot soup is 熱い, older is 年が上, and lots of people is 多い.

para.s: 家の近くに【川】が流れている。
para.why: 小川 is a small river or stream.
para.en: A river flows near my house.

wrong.0: 海 is the sea, not a river.
wrong.1: いけ is a pond; water in a pond doesn't flow.
wrong.2: 道 is a road, not water.

para.why_en: 小川 is a small river or stream, the closest to 川.

options: 川が高くて、のぼれない。
川が降ってきたので、急いで帰った。
川を開けて、部屋に入った。
usage.why: 川 is a river; mountains are climbed, rain falls, and doors are opened.
opts_en: The 'river' is high, so I can't climb it.
In summer I often swam in the river.
A 'river' started falling, so I hurried home.
I opened the 'river' and went into the room.

0.why: You climb a mountain (山).
0.fix: 山が高くて、のぼれない。
0.fix_en: The mountain is high, so I can't climb it.

2.why: What falls from the sky is rain (雨).
2.fix: 雨が降ってきたので、急いで帰った。
2.fix_en: It started raining, so I hurried home.

3.why: You open a door (ドア).
3.fix: ドアを開けて、部屋に入った。
3.fix_en: I opened the door and went into the room.

usage.why_en: 川 is a river; mountains are climbed, rain falls, and doors are opened.

para.s: このスカートは私には少し【長い】。
para.why: 長い is the opposite of みじかい, so みじかくない is closest.
para.en: This skirt is a little long for me.

wrong.1: みじかい means short, the opposite.

para.why_en: 長い is the opposite of みじかい, so みじかくない is closest.

options: 夏休みは冬休みより長い。
usage.why: Height is 背が高い, temperature 高い, and an older brother is 年上.
opts_en: My older sister is 'long' in height.
Summer vacation is longer than winter vacation.
My older brother's age is 'longer' than mine.

0.why: Height uses 高い.
0.fix: 姉は背が高い。
0.fix_en: My older sister is tall.

1.why: Temperature uses 高い.
1.fix: 今日は気おんが高い。
1.fix_en: The temperature is high today.

3.why: Being older is 年が上 / 年上.
3.fix: 兄は私より年が上だ。
3.fix_en: My older brother is older than me.

usage.why_en: Height is 背が高い, temperature is 高い, and being older is 年上 / 年が上.

para.s: 来週、【東京】へ行きます。
para.why: 東京 is the capital (首都) of Japan.
para.en: I'm going to Tokyo next week.

wrong.0: That fits Kyoto or Nara better.
wrong.3: Tokyo is not a small village.

para.why_en: 東京 is the capital (首都) of Japan.

options: 東京の首都は日本です。
東京は人が多くてにぎやかだ。
usage.why: 東京 is a city, the capital of Japan, not a country or a river.
opts_en: The capital of Tokyo is Japan.

0.why: Tokyo is not a country; it is Japan's capital.
0.fix: 東京は日本の首都です。
0.fix_en: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

1.why: Tokyo is a city, not a river.
1.fix: 東京は大きい町です。
1.fix_en: Tokyo is a big city.

2.why: It's the other way round: Japan's capital is Tokyo.
2.fix: 日本の首都は東京です。
2.fix_en: The capital of Japan is Tokyo.

usage.why_en: 東京 is a city, the capital of Japan; it isn't a country or a river.

para.s: 私と兄は【同じ】大学に通っている。
para.why: いっしょの means "the same / shared".
para.en: My brother and I go to the same university.

wrong.0: ちがう means different, the opposite.

para.why_en: いっしょの means 'the same, shared'.

options: 姉と私は同じ服を持っている。
兄と私は年が三つ同じです。
usage.why: 同じ means identical; red and blue, ages three years apart, and one and two are different (ちがう).
opts_en: My older sister and I have the same clothes.
Red and blue are the same color.
My older brother and I are 'the same' by three years.
One and two are the same number.

1.why: Red and blue are different colors (ちがう).
1.fix: 赤と青はちがう色です。
1.fix_en: Red and blue are different colors.

2.why: A three-year gap is a difference (ちがう).
2.fix: 兄と私は年が三つちがう。
2.fix_en: My older brother and I are three years apart.

3.why: One and two are different numbers.
3.fix: 一と二はちがう数です。
3.fix_en: One and two are different numbers.

usage.why_en: 同じ means 'the same'; red and blue, a three-year age gap, and one and two are all different (ちがう).

para.s: この仕事は三年【以上】続けている。
para.why: 以上 means "or more / longer than".
para.en: I've kept up this job for more than three years.

wrong.0: よりみじかく means shorter, the opposite.

para.why_en: 以上 means 'or more / longer than'.

options: 以上で、今日の話を始めます。
二十歳以上の人はお酒が飲めます。
会議には十人以上しか来なかった。
usage.why: 以上 means "or more" or "that's all"; it cannot start a talk, pair with しか, or mean "above" a place.
opts_en: 'That's all' — I'll now begin today's talk.
People twenty and over can drink alcohol.
Only 'ten or more' people came to the meeting.
There is a shop 'above' (ijou) the station.

0.why: 以上 ends a talk ("that's all"); it can't start one.
0.fix: それでは、今日の話を始めます。
0.fix_en: Well then, I'll begin today's talk.

2.why: 以上 (or more) clashes with しか (only); just use the number.
2.fix: 会議には十人しか来なかった。
2.fix_en: Only ten people came to the meeting.

3.why: 以上 is not a place word for "above"; use a place word like 近く.
3.fix: 駅の近くに店がある。
3.fix_en: There is a shop near the station.

usage.why_en: 以上 means "or more" or "that's all"; it can't start a talk, go with しか, or mean "above" a place.

para.s: ここにお【名前】を書いてください。
para.why: しめい (氏名) means one's full name.
para.en: Please write your name here.

wrong.3: 電話番号 is a phone number.

para.why_en: しめい (氏名) means one's full name.

options: 私の名前は二十歳です。
この花の名前を知っていますか。
店の名前は午後九時までです。
usage.why: 名前 is a name, not an age, a color, or opening hours.
opts_en: My name is twenty years old.
Do you know the name of this flower?
The shop's name is until 9 p.m.

0.why: An age belongs to a person, not a name.
0.fix: 私は二十歳です。
0.fix_en: I am twenty years old.

1.why: Brown is a color, not a name.
1.fix: 犬の色は茶色です。
1.fix_en: My dog is brown.

3.why: Opening hours belong to the shop, not its name.
3.fix: 店は午後九時までです。
3.fix_en: The shop is open until 9 p.m.

usage.why_en: 名前 is a name; it can't be an age, a color or opening hours.

para.s: 電車が十分【遅れた】。
para.why: 遅れる means to arrive later than planned.
para.en: The train was ten minutes late.

wrong.0: 早く着く means arrived early, the opposite.

para.why_en: 遅れる means arriving later than planned.

options: 母はいつも遅れて歩く。
昨日は夜遅れまで起きていた。
兄は私より三歳遅れている。
ねぼうして、会社に遅れた。
usage.why: Slow walking is ゆっくり, late at night is 遅く, and being younger is 年下.
opts_en: Yesterday I stayed up until 'being late' at night.
My older brother is three years 'behind' me.
I overslept and was late for work.

0.why: Walking slowly is ゆっくり歩く.
0.fix: 母はいつもゆっくり歩く。
0.fix_en: My mother always walks slowly.

1.why: "Late at night" uses the adverb 遅く.
1.fix: 昨日は夜遅くまで起きていた。
1.fix_en: Yesterday I stayed up until late at night.

2.why: Age differences use 年上/年下, not 遅れる.
2.fix: 兄は私より三歳年上だ。
2.fix_en: My older brother is three years older than me.

usage.why_en: 遅れる means to be late (for something). Walking slowly is ゆっくり, "late at night" is 夜遅く, and age differences use 上/下.

para.s: この【道】をまっすぐ行くと駅です。
para.why: 通り means street / road.
para.en: Go straight along this road and you'll reach the station.
para.why_en: 通り means street or road.

options: 道が分からなくて、人に聞いた。
道で魚がたくさんとれる。
この道はとてもおいしい。
usage.why: 道 is a road; it cannot be bought as books, fished in, or eaten.
opts_en: I didn't know the way, so I asked someone.
Lots of fish can be caught in the road.

1.why: さつ counts books; you can't buy roads.
1.fix: 本を三さつ買った。
1.fix_en: I bought three books.

2.why: Fish are caught in the sea, not on a road.
2.fix: 海で魚がたくさんとれる。
2.fix_en: Lots of fish are caught in the sea.

3.why: Roads aren't eaten; 'tasty' fits food.
3.fix: この料理はとてもおいしい。
3.fix_en: This dish is very tasty.

usage.why_en: 道 is a road or way; it can't be bought like books, fished in, or eaten.

para.s: 夏に家族で北海道を【旅行した】。
para.why: 旅する means to travel.
para.en: In summer my family traveled around Hokkaido.

wrong.0: 引っこす means to move house.
wrong.2: 出ちょう is a business trip, not family travel.

para.why_en: 旅する means to travel.

options: 来月、友達と京都へ旅行に行く。
試験の旅行がよかった。
usage.why: 旅行 is a trip to distant places; a daily walk to the station or a room is not travel.
opts_en: Every morning I 'travel' to the station.
Next month I'm going on a trip to Kyoto with a friend.

0.why: A daily walk to the station isn't a trip.
0.fix: 毎朝、駅まで歩いて行く。
0.fix_en: Every morning I walk to the station.

2.why: Moving around a room isn't travel.
2.fix: 部屋の中を歩いた。
2.fix_en: I walked around inside my room.

3.why: An exam has results (結果), not a trip.
3.fix: 試験の結果がよかった。
3.fix_en: My exam results were good.

usage.why_en: 旅行 is a trip to faraway places; a daily walk to the station or moving around a room is not travel.

para.s: 今日は【非常に】寒い。
para.why: 非常に means "extremely", like とても.
para.en: It's extremely cold today.

wrong.1: 少し means a little, much weaker.
wrong.3: ぜんぜん (with negative) means 'not at all'.

para.why_en: 非常に means 'extremely', like とても.

options: 非常に、明日は休みです。
毎月、非常に一回映画を見ます。
彼の話は非常に面白かった。
この本は非常に二ページしかない。
usage.why: 非常に modifies adjectives (very); it cannot stand alone, count how often, or go with a number of things.
opts_en: Every month I see a movie 'extremely' once.
This book has 'extremely' only two pages.

0.why: 非常に must modify an adjective; it can't start a sentence by itself.
0.fix: 明日は休みです。
0.fix_en: Tomorrow is a day off.

1.why: 非常に can't modify a count like 一回.
1.fix: 毎月一回、映画を見ます。
1.fix_en: I see a movie once a month.

3.why: 非常に means "very" and goes with adjectives or feelings, not with a count like 二ページしかない.
3.fix: この本は二ページしかない。
3.fix_en: This book has only two pages.

usage.why_en: 非常に (extremely) modifies adjectives; it can't stand alone, count how often, or go with a number of things.

para.s: このことは【決して】だれにも言いません。
para.why: 決して〜ない means "never", like 絶対に〜ない.
para.en: I will never tell this to anyone.

wrong.3: もう一度 means once more.

para.why_en: 決して〜ない means 'never', like 絶対に〜ない.

options: 明日、決してパーティーに行きます。
明日は決して晴れるでしょう。
決して、少し待ってください。
この約束は決して忘れません。
usage.why: 決して must be followed by a negative.
opts_en: Tomorrow I will 'never' go to the party.
I will never forget this promise.

0.why: The verb is positive; for "definitely" use 必ず.
0.fix: 明日、必ずパーティーに行きます。
0.fix_en: I'll definitely go to the party tomorrow.

1.why: The verb is positive; for a confident guess use きっと.
1.fix: 明日はきっと晴れるでしょう。
1.fix_en: It will surely be sunny tomorrow.

2.why: 決して can't stand alone as a word to get attention.
2.fix: すみません、少し待ってください。
2.fix_en: Excuse me, please wait a little.

usage.why_en: 決して must be followed by a negative (決して〜ない = never).

para.s: 昨日は十時に【寝ました】。
para.why: 休む can mean going to bed / sleeping.
para.en: Yesterday I went to bed at ten.

wrong.0: 起きる means got up, the opposite.

para.why_en: 休む can mean going to bed / sleeping.

options: 熱があったので、一日中寝ていた。
毎朝七時に寝て、会社へ行く。
いすに寝て、テレビを見た。
赤ちゃんが大きな声で寝ている。
usage.why: 寝る is to sleep; mornings are 起きる, chairs 座る, and loud babies 泣く.
opts_en: I had a fever, so I stayed in bed all day.
Every morning I 'go to sleep' at seven and go to work.
I 'slept' on a chair and watched TV.
The baby is 'sleeping' in a loud voice.

1.why: In the morning before work you get up (起きる).
1.fix: 毎朝七時に起きて、会社へ行く。
1.fix_en: Every morning I get up at seven and go to work.

2.why: On a chair you sit (座る).
2.fix: いすに座って、テレビを見た。
2.fix_en: I sat on a chair and watched TV.

3.why: A loud voice goes with crying (泣く).
3.fix: 赤ちゃんが大きな声で泣いている。
3.fix_en: The baby is crying loudly.

usage.why_en: 寝る is to sleep; mornings are 起きる, chairs are 座る, and loud babies 泣く.

para.s: 毎朝六時に【起きます】。
para.why: 目を覚ます means to wake up.
para.en: I get up at six every morning.

wrong.0: 寝る means to go to bed, the opposite.
wrong.1: 出かける means to go out.
wrong.2: 帰る means to go home.

para.why_en: 目を覚ます means to wake up.

options: 今朝はねぼうして、八時に起きた。
電気が起きて、部屋が明るくなった。
毎朝六時に太陽が起きる。
usage.why: 起きる is waking up; height のびる, lights つく, and the sun のぼる.
opts_en: I overslept this morning and got up at eight.
The light 'woke up' and the room became bright.
The sun 'wakes up' at six every morning.

0.why: Growing taller is 背がのびる.
0.fix: 子供の背がのびた。
0.fix_en: My child got taller.

2.why: A light coming on is つく.
2.fix: 電気がついて、部屋が明るくなった。
2.fix_en: The light came on and the room became bright.

3.why: The sun rises: のぼる.
3.fix: 毎朝六時に太陽がのぼる。
3.fix_en: The sun rises at six every morning.

usage.why_en: 起きる is waking or getting up; height のびる, lights つく, and the sun のぼる.

para.s: どうぞ、こちらに【座って】ください。
para.why: おかけになる is the polite way to ask someone to sit.
para.en: Please sit here.

wrong.1: 立つ means stand, the opposite.

para.why_en: おかけになる is the polite way to ask someone to sit.

options: 自転車に座って学校へ行った。
電車で席が空いていたので座った。
毎朝、駅まで座って行く。
usage.why: 座る is to sit; birds fly, bikes are ridden (乗る), and getting to the station is 歩く.
opts_en: A bird is sitting in the sky.
There was a free seat on the train, so I sat down.
Every morning I go to the station 'sitting'.

0.why: There's nothing to sit on in the sky; birds fly there.
0.fix: 鳥が空を飛んでいる。
0.fix_en: A bird is flying in the sky.

1.why: Riding a bike is 乗る.
1.fix: 自転車に乗って学校へ行った。
1.fix_en: I rode my bike to school.

3.why: You can't travel by sitting; going on foot is 歩く.
3.fix: 毎朝、駅まで歩いて行く。
3.fix_en: Every morning I walk to the station.

usage.why_en: 座る means to sit; birds fly, bikes are ridden (乗る), and going on foot is 歩く.

para.s: 【飛行機】でおおさかから東京へ行った。
para.why: An airplane is a vehicle that flies in the sky.
para.en: I went from Osaka to Tokyo by plane.

wrong.3: That is a car or bus.

para.why_en: An airplane is a vehicle that flies in the sky.

options: 飛行機に乗って、次の駅で降りた。
飛行機で家から学校まで走った。
飛行機の窓から白いくもが見えた。
usage.why: Stations are for trains, fishing is done from boats, and short rides to school are by bicycle.
opts_en: I took a plane and got off at the next station.
I caught fish from a plane.
I ran from home to school by plane.
I could see white clouds from the airplane window.

0.why: Getting off at the next station means a train.
0.fix: 電車に乗って、次の駅で降りた。
0.fix_en: I took a train and got off at the next station.

1.why: You fish from a boat: 船.
1.fix: 船で魚をとった。
1.fix_en: I caught fish from a boat.

2.why: Getting from home to school is by bicycle, not plane.
2.fix: 自転車で家から学校まで走った。
2.fix_en: I rode my bike from home to school.

usage.why_en: Stations are for trains, fishing is done from boats, and short trips to school are by bicycle.

para.s: 雨の中、試合を【続けた】。
para.why: 続ける means to keep going and not stop.
para.en: We continued the match in the rain.

wrong.0: やめた means stopped, the opposite.
wrong.1: 始めなかった means it never began.
wrong.3: 休んだ means took a break.

para.why_en: 続ける means to keep going and not stop.

options: 毎日、日本語の勉強を続けています。
雨が三日も続けている。
会議が五時まで続けた。
昨日で仕事を続けたので、今日から休みです。
usage.why: 続ける is transitive; rain and meetings 続く, and stopping work is やめる.
opts_en: I keep studying Japanese every day.
The rain has been 'continuing (something)' for three days.
I 'continued' my job until yesterday, so I'm off from today.

1.why: Rain continues by itself, so use the intransitive 続く.
1.fix: 雨が三日も続いている。
1.fix_en: It has been raining for three whole days.

2.why: With が and no object, use 続く.
2.fix: 会議が五時まで続いた。
2.fix_en: The meeting went on until five.

3.why: Being off from today means you stopped working (やめる).
3.fix: 昨日で仕事をやめたので、今日から休みです。
3.fix_en: I quit my job as of yesterday, so I'm off from today.

usage.why_en: 続ける is transitive (〜を続ける); rain and meetings 続く, and stopping work is やめる.

para.s: 【今日】は日曜日です。
para.why: 本日 is the formal word for today.
para.en: Today is Sunday.
para.why_en: 本日 is the formal word for today.

options: 今日、来週の会議に出席しました。
今日は朝から雨が降っている。
今日は今年の一月です。
usage.why: 今日 is this day; frequency is 一日に, and the current month is 今月.
opts_en: It has been raining since this morning.

0.why: Next week's meeting hasn't happened yet, so you can't have attended it today.
0.fix: 今日、会議に出席しました。
0.fix_en: I attended a meeting today.

2.why: "Once a day" is 一日に一回.
2.fix: 一日に一回、薬を飲む。
2.fix_en: I take medicine once a day.

3.why: A month is 今月 (this month), not 今日 (this day).
3.fix: 今月は一月です。
3.fix_en: This month is January.

usage.why_en: 今日 means this day; frequency is 一日に, and the current month is 今月.

para.s: 東京での【生活】にはもう慣れた。
para.why: 暮らし means daily life.
para.en: I've already gotten used to life in Tokyo.
para.why_en: 暮らし means daily life.

options: 一人の生活は楽しいけど、少しさびしい。
usage.why: 生活 is one's way of life, not a name or an object.
opts_en: Living alone is fun, but a little lonely.

0.why: A name is 名前, not 生活.
0.fix: 私の名前は田中です。
0.fix_en: My name is Tanaka.

1.why: 生活 isn't a thing you can buy.
1.fix: りんごを三つ買った。
1.fix_en: I bought three apples.

3.why: 生活 isn't an object you can sit on.
3.fix: いすに座った。
3.fix_en: I sat on a chair.

usage.why_en: 生活 is one's daily life or way of living, not a name or an object.

para.s: 【日本】は山が多い国です。
para.why: For a speaker in Japan, この国 means Japan.
para.en: Japan is a mountainous country.

wrong.0: アメリカ is a different country.
wrong.2: 中国 is China, a different country.
wrong.3: 外国 means foreign countries, not Japan.

para.why_en: For a speaker in Japan, この国 (this country) means Japan.

options: 日本は東京の首都です。
日本では、家に入るときにくつをぬぐ。
usage.why: 日本 is a country; Tokyo is its capital, and a Japanese person is 日本人.
opts_en: Japan is the capital of Tokyo.
In Japan, you take off your shoes when you go into a house.

0.why: It's the other way round: Tokyo is Japan's capital.
0.fix: 東京は日本の首都です。
0.fix_en: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

1.why: Japan is a country, not a town.
1.fix: 日本はアジアの国です。
1.fix_en: Japan is a country in Asia.

2.why: A person from Japan is 日本人.
2.fix: 私は日本人です。
2.fix_en: I am Japanese.

usage.why_en: 日本 is a country; Tokyo is its capital, and a Japanese person is 日本人.

para.s: 【次】は田中さんの番です。
para.why: 今度 can mean "next (time)".
para.en: Next is Mr. Tanaka's turn.
para.why_en: 今度 can mean 'next (time)'.

options: 次の駅で乗りかえてください。
次の日に、昨日の会議があった。
この料理は次においしい。
次で寒いので、窓を閉めた。
usage.why: 次 means the next one in order; it does not mean "very" or "because".
opts_en: Please change trains at the next station.
'The next day', there was yesterday's meeting.
It's cold 'by next', so I closed the window.

1.why: 'The next day' and 'yesterday's meeting' clash in time.
1.fix: 次の日に、また会議があった。
1.fix_en: The next day, there was another meeting.

2.why: 次 doesn't mean 'very'.
2.fix: この料理はとてもおいしい。
2.fix_en: This dish is very tasty.

3.why: 次で doesn't give a reason; ので already does.
3.fix: 寒いので、窓を閉めた。
3.fix_en: It was cold, so I closed the window.

usage.why_en: 次 means the next one in order; it doesn't mean 'very' or 'because'.

para.s: りんごを【一つ】ください。
para.why: 一こ is the counter for small round things like apples.
para.en: One apple, please.

wrong.0: 一本 counts long thin things.

para.why_en: 一こ is the counter for small round things like apples.

options: このケーキを一つください。
毎週一つ、プールへ行く。
usage.why: People are counted 一人, times 一回, and animals 一ぴき.
opts_en: Every week I go to the pool 'one (thing)'.
There is 'one (thing)' dog in the room.

0.why: People are counted with 人.
0.fix: 私は兄が一人います。
0.fix_en: I have one older brother.

2.why: Times are counted with 回.
2.fix: 毎週一回、プールへ行く。
2.fix_en: I go to the pool once a week.

3.why: Small animals are counted with ひき.
3.fix: 部屋に犬が一ぴきいる。
3.fix_en: There is one dog in the room.

usage.why_en: People are counted 一人, times 一回, and small animals 一ぴき; 一つ is for things.

para.s: 今週は仕事が【忙しい】。
para.why: 忙しい means having no free time.
para.en: I'm busy with work this week.

wrong.1: ひまだ means free, the opposite.
wrong.3: 少ない means there is little work.

para.why_en: 忙しい means having no free time.

options: 日曜日は何もすることがなくて、忙しい。
忙しいので、テレビを見てのんびりしている。
年末は忙しくて、休みがとれない。
この部屋は忙しいので、静かだ。
usage.why: 忙しい means busy; having nothing to do and relaxing are ひま.
opts_en: On Sunday I have nothing to do, so I'm busy.
I'm busy, so I'm relaxing watching TV.
The end of the year is busy, and I can't take time off.
This room is busy, so it's quiet.

0.why: Nothing to do means free (ひま), not busy.
0.fix: 日曜日は何もすることがなくて、ひまだ。
0.fix_en: On Sunday I have nothing to do, so I'm free.

1.why: If you're relaxing, you're free (ひま), not busy.
1.fix: ひまなので、テレビを見てのんびりしている。
1.fix_en: I'm free, so I'm relaxing in front of the TV.

3.why: A room can't be busy, and busy doesn't lead to quiet.
3.fix: この部屋は人が少ないので、静かだ。
3.fix_en: There are few people in this room, so it's quiet.

usage.why_en: 忙しい means busy; having nothing to do and relaxing are ひま.

para.s: 夏休みに【両親】に会いに帰った。
para.why: 両親 means one's father and mother.
para.en: During summer vacation I went home to see my parents.
para.why_en: 両親 means one's father and mother.

options: 私の両親は三人います。
両親の一人は私の兄です。
両親は北海道に住んでいる。
usage.why: 両親 are exactly two people, one's father and mother.
opts_en: One of my parents is my older brother.
My parents are younger than me.

0.why: 両親 is always two people; for everyone at home say 家族.
0.fix: 私の家族は三人です。
0.fix_en: There are three people in my family.

1.why: Your brother can't be one of your parents.
1.fix: 兄は両親と住んでいる。
1.fix_en: My older brother lives with our parents.

2.why: Parents are always older than their child.
2.fix: 両親は私より背が低い。
2.fix_en: My parents are shorter than me.

usage.why_en: 両親 means exactly two people: one's father and mother.

para.s: この学校には【生徒】が五百人いる。
para.why: 生徒 are pupils at a school.
para.en: This school has five hundred pupils.
para.why_en: 生徒 are pupils at a school (学生).

options: 先生は生徒たちに宿題を出した。
病院には生徒がたくさん入院している。
この店の生徒はとても親切だ。
生徒が先生にじゅぎょうを教えている。
usage.why: 生徒 are pupils who learn; hospital patients and shop staff are different.
opts_en: The teacher gave the students homework.
Many pupils are hospitalized in the hospital.
The pupils at this shop are very kind.
The pupils are teaching the class to the teacher.

1.why: People staying in a hospital are patients (かんじゃ).
1.fix: 病院にはかんじゃがたくさん入院している。
1.fix_en: Many patients are staying in the hospital.

2.why: People working in a shop are 店員.
2.fix: この店の店員はとても親切だ。
2.fix_en: The staff at this shop are very kind.

3.why: Pupils learn; it's the teacher who teaches.
3.fix: 先生が生徒に英語を教えている。
3.fix_en: The teacher is teaching the pupils English.

usage.why_en: 生徒 are pupils who learn at school; hospital patients and shop staff are different.

para.s: 駅の近くに新しい【店】ができた。
para.why: ショップ is a loanword for shop.
para.en: A new shop opened near the station.
para.why_en: ショップ is a loanword for shop.

options: 熱があるので、店でみてもらった。
この店のパンはとてもおいしい。
usage.why: Doctors are at hospitals, trains leave from stations, and you sleep at home.
opts_en: I had a fever, so I got checked at a 'shop'.
I got on a train from a 'shop'.
The bread at this shop is really good.
Every night I sleep at a 'shop'.

0.why: Doctors are at a hospital.
0.fix: 熱があるので、病院でみてもらった。
0.fix_en: I have a fever, so I got checked at the hospital.

1.why: Trains leave from a station.

3.why: You sleep at home.
3.fix: 毎晩、家で寝ている。
3.fix_en: I sleep at home every night.

usage.why_en: Doctors are at hospitals, trains leave from stations, and you sleep at home.

para.s: 今朝はいつもより【早く】起きた。
para.why: 早めに means "earlier than usual".
para.en: This morning I got up earlier than usual.

wrong.0: おそく means late, the opposite.
wrong.3: 長く means for a long time.

para.why_en: 早めに means 'earlier than usual'.

options: 試験が早くて、答えられなかった。
夜早くまで起きていた。
朝早く起きて、散歩に行った。
usage.why: A hard test is 難しい, late at night is 遅く, and older is 年上.
opts_en: The exam was 'early', so I couldn't answer.
I stayed up until 'early' at night.
My father is three 'earlier' than my mother.
I got up early in the morning and went for a walk.

0.why: Not being able to answer means the test was hard (難しい).
0.fix: 試験が難しくて、答えられなかった。
0.fix_en: The exam was hard, so I couldn't answer.

1.why: Staying up at night is 遅くまで (until late).
1.fix: 夜遅くまで起きていた。
1.fix_en: I stayed up until late at night.

2.why: Being older is 年上.
2.fix: 父は母より三つ年上だ。
2.fix_en: My father is three years older than my mother.

usage.why_en: A hard test is 難しい, late at night is 遅く, and older is 年上.

para.s: 駅は人で【いっぱい】だ。
para.why: 人でいっぱい means crowded (こんでいる).
para.en: The station is full of people.

wrong.0: すいている means empty, the opposite.

para.why_en: 人でいっぱい means crowded (こんでいる).

options: もうおなかがいっぱいで、何も食べられない。
かばんがいっぱいなので、まだたくさん入る。
部屋はいっぱいで、だれもいない。
ちゅうしゃじょうはいっぱいなので、すぐに車を止められた。
usage.why: いっぱい means full; a full bag, room or car park has no space left.
opts_en: I'm already full and can't eat anything.
My bag is full, so lots more will still fit.
The room is full, and there's nobody in it.
The parking lot is full, so I could park right away.

1.why: If more fits, the bag isn't full; it's big.
1.fix: かばんが大きいので、まだたくさん入る。
1.fix_en: My bag is big, so lots more will still fit.

2.why: A full room can't have nobody in it.
2.fix: 部屋はしずかで、だれもいない。
2.fix_en: The room is quiet; there's nobody in it.

3.why: You can park at once only if the lot is empty: すいている.
3.fix: ちゅうしゃじょうはすいていたので、すぐに車を止められた。
3.fix_en: The parking lot was empty, so I could park right away.

usage.why_en: いっぱい means full. A full bag, room or parking lot has no space left.

para.s: 週末に【映画】を見に行った。
para.why: ムービー is a loanword meaning movie.
para.en: On the weekend I went to see a movie.
para.why_en: ムービー is a loanword meaning movie.

options: 映画を読んで、感想を書いた。
この映画を見て、ないてしまった。
usage.why: 映画 is watched (見る); it cannot be read, worn or written with.
opts_en: I 'read' a movie and wrote my thoughts on it.
I watched this movie and ended up crying.
I put on a movie and went out.
I wrote a letter with a movie.

0.why: Movies are watched (見る), not read.
0.fix: 映画を見て、感想を書いた。
0.fix_en: I watched a movie and wrote my thoughts on it.

2.why: You put on clothes, like a coat.
2.fix: コートを着て出かけた。
2.fix_en: I put on a coat and went out.

3.why: You write with a pen.
3.fix: ペンで手紙を書いた。
3.fix_en: I wrote a letter with a pen.

usage.why_en: 映画 is watched (見る); it can't be read, worn, or written with.

para.s: 【二人】で旅行に行った。
para.why: 二人 means two people, for example a friend and me.
para.en: The two of us went on a trip.

wrong.1: 一人 is just one person.
wrong.2: 家族みんな is usually more than two.

para.why_en: 二人 means two people, for example a friend and me.

options: 兄弟は二人で、兄と姉と弟がいる。
うちには二人の犬がいる。
二人で写真をとりましょう。
ケーキを二人ください。
usage.why: 二人 counts two people; three siblings, dogs (二ひき) and cakes (二つ) are wrong.
opts_en: I have 'two' siblings: an older brother, an older sister and a younger brother.
Let's take a photo of the two of us.

0.why: Three siblings are listed, so it's 三人.
0.fix: 兄弟は三人で、兄と姉と弟がいる。
0.fix_en: I have three siblings: an older brother, an older sister and a younger brother.

1.why: Dogs are counted with ひき, not 人.
1.fix: うちには犬が二ひきいる。
1.fix_en: We have two dogs at home.

3.why: Cakes are things, so use 二つ.
3.fix: ケーキを二つください。
3.fix_en: Two pieces of cake, please.

usage.why_en: 二人 counts two people; three siblings, dogs (二ひき) and cakes (二つ) don't fit.

para.s: 夏はよく海で【泳いだ】。
para.why: 水泳 means swimming.
para.en: In summer I often swam in the sea.
para.why_en: 水泳 means swimming.

options: プールで一時間泳いだ。
usage.why: 泳ぐ happens in water; birds fly, and on land we walk or drive.
opts_en: A bird is swimming in the sky.
Cars are swimming along the road.
I swam in the pool for an hour.

0.why: Birds in the sky fly (飛ぶ).
0.fix: 鳥が空を飛んでいる。
0.fix_en: A bird is flying in the sky.

1.why: You go to the station on land, e.g. on foot (歩く).
1.fix: 駅まで歩いて行った。
1.fix_en: I walked to the station.

2.why: Cars on a road run (走る).
2.fix: 車が道を走っている。
2.fix_en: Cars are driving along the road.

usage.why_en: 泳ぐ happens in water; birds fly, and on land people walk and cars drive (走る).

para.s: お金は【十分】あります。
para.why: たっぷり means plenty.
para.en: I have enough money.

wrong.1: ぜんぜん means not at all.
wrong.3: ちょっと means a bit.

para.why_en: たっぷり means plenty.

options: 時間は十分あるから、急がなくてもいい。
十分なので、もう少しください。
十分食べたので、おなかがすいた。
十分寝たので、とても眠い。
usage.why: 十分 means enough, so you do not want more, are not hungry and are not sleepy.
opts_en: There's plenty of time, so you don't need to hurry.
It's enough, so please give me a little more.
I ate enough, so I got hungry.
I slept enough, so I'm very sleepy.

1.why: If you want more, it isn't enough: 足りない.
1.fix: 足りないので、もう少しください。
1.fix_en: It's not enough, so please give me a little more.

2.why: Eating enough makes you full, not hungry.
2.fix: 十分食べたので、おなかがいっぱいだ。
2.fix_en: I ate plenty, so I'm full.

3.why: Sleeping enough makes you feel rested, not sleepy.
3.fix: 十分寝たので、とても元気だ。
3.fix_en: I slept plenty, so I feel great.

usage.why_en: 十分 means enough. If you have enough you don't ask for more, and after eating or sleeping enough you aren't hungry or sleepy.

para.s: 明日、サッカーの【試合】がある。
para.why: ゲーム (game / match) means the same.
para.en: There's a soccer match tomorrow.

wrong.2: じゅぎょう is a class.

para.why_en: ゲーム (game / match) means the same.

options: 英語の試合に合格した。
けっこんの試合に出た。
usage.why: 試合 is a sports match; language tests are 試験 and weddings are 式.
opts_en: I mailed a letter at the match.

0.why: A language test is 試験.
0.fix: 英語の試験に合格した。
0.fix_en: I passed the English exam.

2.why: A wedding ceremony is けっこん式.
2.fix: けっこん式に出た。
2.fix_en: I attended a wedding.

3.why: Letters are mailed at the post office (郵便局).
3.fix: 郵便局で手紙を出した。
3.fix_en: I mailed a letter at the post office.

usage.why_en: 試合 is a sports match or game; language tests are 試験, and a wedding is a 式 (ceremony).

para.s: 母の【顔】を見て安心した。
para.why: 表情 means facial expression.
para.en: Seeing my mother's face, I felt relieved.
para.why_en: 表情 means facial expression.

usage.why: Music is heard with ears, shoes go on feet, and writing is done with hands.
opts_en: I listened to music with my 'face'.
I got up in the morning and washed my face.

0.why: You hear with your ears (耳).
0.fix: 耳で音楽を聞いた。
0.fix_en: I listened to music with my ears.

1.why: Shoes go on your feet (足).
1.fix: 足にくつをはいた。
1.fix_en: I put shoes on my feet.

3.why: You write with your hand (手).
3.fix: 手で字を書いた。
3.fix_en: I wrote letters by hand.

usage.why_en: Music is heard with ears, shoes go on feet, and writing is done with hands.

para.s: 【目】が悪いので、めがねをかけている。
para.why: 目が悪い means poor eyesight (しりょく).
para.en: My eyes are bad, so I wear glasses.
para.why_en: 目が悪い means poor eyesight (しりょく).

options: 目を閉じて、音楽を聞いた。
usage.why: Eyes see; ears hear, legs walk, and the nose smells.
opts_en: I heard the sound with my eyes.
I smelled it with my eyes.
I closed my eyes and listened to music.

0.why: You hear with your ears (耳).
0.fix: 耳で音を聞いた。
0.fix_en: I heard the sound with my ears.

1.why: You walk with your feet (足).
1.fix: 足で歩いた。
1.fix_en: I walked on my feet.

2.why: You smell with your nose (鼻).
2.fix: 鼻でにおいをかいだ。
2.fix_en: I smelled it with my nose.

usage.why_en: Eyes are for seeing; you hear with your ears, walk with your legs and smell with your nose.

para.s: コーヒーにさとうを【入れます】か。
para.why: 加える means to add (something into something).

para.why_en: 加える means to add something into something.

options: 電車に入れて、会社へ行った。
毎朝、シャワーを入れてから出かける。
usage.why: 入れる is putting something inside; trains are 乗る, windows しめる, and showers あびる.
opts_en: I put a book in my bag.
I 'put in' the train and went to work.
It was cold, so I 'put in' the window.
Every morning I 'put in' a shower before going out.

1.why: You ride a train: 電車に乗る.
1.fix: 電車に乗って、会社へ行った。
1.fix_en: I took the train to work.

2.why: When it's cold you close the window: 閉める.
2.fix: 寒いので、窓を閉めた。
2.fix_en: It was cold, so I closed the window.

3.why: Taking a shower is シャワーをあびる.
3.fix: 毎朝、シャワーをあびてから出かける。
3.fix_en: Every morning I take a shower before going out.

usage.why_en: 入れる is putting something inside. You ride (乗る) a train, close (閉める) a window, and take (あびる) a shower.

para.s: 寝る前に【音楽】を聞く。
para.why: 曲 means a piece of music / song.

wrong.0: ニュース is the news.
wrong.1: 話 is a talk or story.

para.why_en: 曲 means a piece of music or song.

options: 音楽を読んで、感想を書いた。
音楽を聞きながら、勉強する。
音楽を飲みながら、休んだ。
usage.why: 音楽 is listened to (聞く), not read, drunk or used to wash.
opts_en: I 'read' music and wrote my thoughts on it.
I study while listening to music.
I washed my face with music.

0.why: Music is listened to (聞く), not read.
0.fix: 音楽を聞いて、感想を書いた。
0.fix_en: I listened to music and wrote my thoughts on it.

2.why: You drink a drink, like tea.
2.fix: お茶を飲みながら、休んだ。
2.fix_en: I rested while drinking tea.

3.why: You wash your face with water.
3.fix: 水で顔を洗った。
3.fix_en: I washed my face with water.

usage.why_en: 音楽 is listened to (聞く); it can't be read, drunk, or used for washing.

para.s: 何かいい【手】はありませんか。
para.why: Here 手 means a way or method (方法).
para.en: Isn't there some good way?

options: 食事の前に手を洗いましょう。
usage.why: Ears hear, feet wear shoes, and eyes close for sleep.
opts_en: I listened to music with my 'hands'.
Let's wash our hands before eating.

0.why: You hear with your ears (耳).
0.fix: 耳で音楽を聞いた。
0.fix_en: I listened to music with my ears.

1.why: Shoes go on your feet (足).
1.fix: 足にくつをはいた。
1.fix_en: I put shoes on my feet.

3.why: You close your eyes (目) to sleep.
3.fix: 目を閉じて寝た。
3.fix_en: I closed my eyes and slept.

usage.why_en: Ears hear, feet wear shoes, and eyes close for sleep.

para.s: このいすは【木】で作られている。
para.why: もくざい means wood as a material.

para.why_en: もくざい means wood as a material.

options: 公園の木の下でおべんとうを食べた。
usage.why: Trees do not cry, run, or count as books.
opts_en: The tree is crying out (like an animal).
I bought three (bound volumes of) trees.
We ate our boxed lunch under a tree in the park.

0.why: 鳴く is for animal sounds, e.g. birds.
0.fix: 鳥が鳴いている。
0.fix_en: A bird is singing.

1.why: さつ counts books.
1.fix: 本を三さつ買った。
1.fix_en: I bought three books.

2.why: Trees can't run; animals can.
2.fix: 犬が走っている。
2.fix_en: A dog is running.

usage.why_en: Trees don't make animal sounds or run, and さつ is the counter for books.

para.s: 昨日のパーティーは【楽しかった】。

wrong.0: つまらない means boring, the opposite.

試験に落ちて、楽しかった。
かぜをひいて、とても楽しい。
usage.why: 楽しい describes enjoyable experiences; failing and colds are not fun, and cake is おいしい.

2.why: Food is described by taste: おいしい.
2.fix: このケーキはおいしい。
2.fix_en: This cake is delicious.

3.why: A cold makes you feel awful: つらい.
3.fix: かぜをひいて、とてもつらい。
3.fix_en: I caught a cold and feel awful.

usage.why_en: 楽しい describes enjoyable experiences. Failing and colds aren't fun, and good-tasting cake is おいしい.

para.s: なくしたかぎをやっと【見つけた】。
para.why: 発見する means to find / discover.
para.en: I finally found the key I lost.

wrong.0: なくす means lost, the opposite.
wrong.2: 探す means searched, not necessarily found.

para.why_en: 発見する means to find or discover.

usage.why: 見つける is transitive (〜を見つける); with が use 見つかる; newspapers are 読む, waiting is 待つ.
opts_en: I found a good restaurant near the station.
I 'found' my friend at the station for an hour.

0.why: A daily newspaper is read (読む).
0.fix: 毎朝、新聞を読む。
0.fix_en: I read the newspaper every morning.

2.why: With が and no object, use the intransitive 見つかる.
2.fix: かぎが見つかった。
2.fix_en: The key turned up.

3.fix: 友達を駅で一時間待った。
3.fix_en: I waited an hour for my friend at the station.

usage.why_en: 見つける is transitive (〜を見つける); with が use 見つかる. Newspapers are read (読む), and waiting is 待つ.

para.s: 弟は【一生けんめい】勉強している。

試験に合格するために、一生けんめい勉強した。
このケーキは一生けんめいおいしい。

'With all my effort', I did nothing.
I studied as hard as I could to pass the exam.
This cake is 'with all its effort' delicious.

0.why: Weather isn't something you put effort into.
0.fix: たぶん、明日は雨です。
0.fix_en: It will probably rain tomorrow.

1.why: You can't try hard at doing nothing.
1.fix: 一日中、何もしなかった。
1.fix_en: I did nothing all day.

3.why: Taste isn't effort; use とても for "very".
3.fix: このケーキはとてもおいしい。
3.fix_en: This cake is very delicious.

usage.why_en: 一生けんめい describes putting all your effort into an action, not the weather, doing nothing, or taste.

para.s: 弟は今年十【歳】になる。
para.why: 才 is the simpler way of writing the age counter 歳.
para.en: My younger brother turns ten this year.

wrong.0: 年 counts years, not age in this form.

para.why_en: 才 is the simpler way of writing the age counter 歳.

options: このビルは五十歳です。
りんごを三歳ください。
祖父は今年八十歳になった。
usage.why: 歳 counts people's ages; buildings are 年, apples つ/こ, and durations 時間.
opts_en: This building is fifty 'years old' (as a person's age).
Please give me three 'years old' of apples.
The meeting took three 'years of age'.
My grandfather turned eighty this year.

0.why: 歳 is for people's ages; a building's age is counted in 年.
0.fix: このビルは五十年前にできた。
0.fix_en: This building was built fifty years ago.

1.why: Apples are counted with つ or こ.
1.fix: りんごを三つください。
1.fix_en: Three apples, please.

2.why: Length of time uses 時間.
2.fix: 会議は三時間かかった。
2.fix_en: The meeting took three hours.

usage.why_en: 歳 counts people's ages; buildings use 年, apples つ/こ, and lengths of time 時間.

para.s: 引っこしを【手伝って】くれてありがとう。
para.why: 助ける means to help.
para.en: Thank you for helping me move.
para.why_en: 助ける means to help.

options: 母が料理を作るのを手伝った。
先生にお金を手伝った。
病気が手伝って、元気になった。
犬を手伝って公園へ行った。
usage.why: 手伝う is helping with a task; lending money is 貸す, recovering is 治る, and taking a dog is 連れる.
opts_en: The illness 'helped', and I got well.
I 'helped' my dog to the park.

1.why: Giving money to be returned is lending: 貸す.
1.fix: 先生にお金を貸した。
1.fix_en: I lent money to my teacher.

2.why: An illness getting better is 治る.
2.fix: 病気が治って、元気になった。
2.fix_en: My illness got better, and I was well again.

3.why: Taking a dog with you is 連れる.
3.fix: 犬を連れて公園へ行った。
3.fix_en: I took my dog to the park.

usage.why_en: 手伝う is helping someone with a task. Lending money is 貸す, getting better is 治る, and taking a dog along is 連れる.

para.s: みんなの【意見】を聞いてから決めましょう。
para.why: 意見 means one's opinion or idea (考え).
para.en: Let's decide after hearing everyone's opinions.
para.why_en: 意見 means one's opinion or idea (考え).

options: 会議で自分の意見を言った。
意見に乗って会社へ行った。
usage.why: 意見 is an opinion; it cannot be bought, drunk or ridden.
opts_en: I gave my opinion at the meeting.

0.why: You can't buy opinions; 本 counts things like pens.
0.fix: ペンを三本買った。
0.fix_en: I bought three pens.

2.why: You drink a drink, like coffee.
2.fix: 毎朝、コーヒーを飲む。
2.fix_en: I drink coffee every morning.

3.why: You ride a vehicle, like a train.
3.fix: 電車に乗って会社へ行った。
3.fix_en: I took the train to work.

usage.why_en: 意見 is an opinion; it can't be bought, drunk, or ridden.

para.s: 受付に【女性】が二人いる。

para.en: There are two women at reception.
para.why_en: 女性 means a woman (女の人).

options: 兄は女性なので、ネクタイをしている。
この会社では、たくさんの女性が働いている。
私の祖父は九十歳の女性です。
usage.why: 女性 is a woman; a father, brother and grandfather are men (男性).
opts_en: My older brother is a 'woman', so he wears a tie.
Many women work at this company.

0.why: A father is a man (男性).
0.fix: 父はやさしい男性だ。
0.fix_en: My father is a kind man.

1.why: A brother is a man, and wearing a tie fits a company worker.
1.fix: 兄は会社員なので、ネクタイをしている。
1.fix_en: My older brother is an office worker, so he wears a tie.

3.why: A grandfather is a man (男性).
3.fix: 私の祖父は九十歳の男性です。

0.fix: 熱が出たので、医者にみてもらった。
0.fix_en: I had a fever, so I saw a doctor.

1.why: You withdraw money at a bank.
1.fix: 銀行でお金を下ろした。
1.fix_en: I withdrew money at the bank.

2.why: You borrow books at a library.
2.fix: 図書館で本を借りた。
2.fix_en: I borrowed a book at the library.

usage.why_en: The police handle things like lost property; doctors, banks and libraries are other places.

para.s: 来月、駅前でコンサートが【開かれる】。
para.why: 開かれる means an event is held (行われる).
para.en: Next month a concert will be held in front of the station.

wrong.1: 中止 means canceled, the opposite.
wrong.3: 決まる means to be decided.

para.why_en: 開かれる means an event is held (行われる).

options: 教科書の十ページを開いてください。
電気を開いて、部屋を明るくした。
テレビを開いて、ニュースを見た。
雨がやんで、空が開いた。
usage.why: 開く is for books and events; lights and TVs are つける, and the sky 晴れる.
opts_en: Please open your textbook to page ten.
I 'opened' the light and brightened the room.
I 'opened' the TV and watched the news.
The rain stopped, and the sky 'opened'.

1.why: Lights are turned on: つける.
1.fix: 電気をつけて、部屋を明るくした。
1.fix_en: I turned on the light and brightened the room.

2.why: A TV is turned on: つける.
2.fix: テレビをつけて、ニュースを見た。
2.fix_en: I turned on the TV and watched the news.

3.why: The sky clearing up is 晴れる.
3.fix: 雨がやんで、空が晴れた。
3.fix_en: The rain stopped, and the sky cleared.

usage.why_en: 開く is for things like books, doors and events. Lights and TVs are turned on (つける), and the sky clears (晴れる).

para.s: 時間がないので【急いで】ください。
para.why: 急ぐ means to hurry (do it quickly).
para.en: There's no time, so please hurry.

wrong.0: ゆっくり means slowly, the opposite.

para.why_en: 急ぐ means to hurry (do it quickly).

options: 時間がたくさんあるので、急いでください。
電車に遅れそうなので、駅まで急いだ。
急いでいるので、ゆっくり歩こう。
この時計は急いでいる。
usage.why: 急ぐ is hurrying; with lots of time you need not hurry, and a fast clock 進んでいる.
opts_en: There's plenty of time, so please hurry.
I was about to miss the train, so I hurried to the station.
I'm in a hurry, so let's walk slowly.

0.why: With plenty of time, there's no need to hurry.
0.fix: 時間がたくさんあるので、急がなくてもいいです。
0.fix_en: There's plenty of time, so you don't need to hurry.

2.why: Being in a hurry clashes with walking slowly.
2.fix: 急いでいるので、走ろう。
2.fix_en: I'm in a hurry, so let's run.

3.why: A clock that runs fast 進んでいる.
3.fix: この時計は進んでいる。
3.fix_en: This clock is fast.

usage.why_en: 急ぐ means to hurry; with plenty of time you don't need to hurry, and a fast clock 進んでいる.

para.s: このくつはもう【古い】。
para.why: 古い means old, not new.
para.en: These shoes are already old.

wrong.1: 新しい means new, the opposite.
wrong.2: 若い is for people's age, not things.

para.why_en: 古い means old, i.e. not new.

options: 祖父は八十歳で、とても古い。
この町には古い建物が多い。
この店は先週できたばかりで、とても古い。
usage.why: People are 年をとった/若い, and a shop opened last week is 新しい.
opts_en: My grandfather is eighty and very 'old' (like an object).
My little brother is three and still 'old'.
There are many old buildings in this town.
This shop just opened last week, so it's very 'old'.

0.why: 古い is for things; for people say 年をとっている.
0.fix: 祖父は八十歳で、もう年をとっている。
0.fix_en: My grandfather is eighty and is getting on in years.

1.why: A three-year-old is still small (小さい), not old.
1.fix: 弟は三歳で、まだ小さい。
1.fix_en: My little brother is three and still small.

3.why: A shop that just opened is new (新しい).
3.fix: この店は先週できたばかりで、とても新しい。
3.fix_en: This shop just opened last week, so it's very new.

usage.why_en: 古い is for things; people are 年をとった or 若い, and a shop opened last week is 新しい.

para.s: 赤ちゃんがぐっすり【眠って】いる。
para.why: 寝る means to sleep.
para.en: The baby is sleeping soundly.

wrong.0: 起きる means awake, the opposite.

para.why_en: 寝る means to sleep, like 眠る.

options: 毎朝七時に眠って、会社へ行く。
眠いので、コーヒーを飲んで眠った。
昨日は疲れて、十時間も眠った。
usage.why: 眠る is sleeping; mornings mean 起きる, coffee wakes you up, and rain 降る.
opts_en: Every morning I fall asleep at seven and go to work.
I was sleepy, so I drank coffee and fell asleep.
I was tired yesterday and slept for a full ten hours.

0.why: Before going to work you get up (起きる).
0.fix: 毎朝七時に起きて、会社へ行く。
0.fix_en: Every morning I get up at seven and go to work.

1.why: Coffee wakes you up; it doesn't put you to sleep.
1.fix: 眠いので、コーヒーを飲んだ。
1.fix_en: I was sleepy, so I drank some coffee.

2.why: Rain falls (降る); it can't sleep.
2.fix: 雨が降っている。
2.fix_en: It's raining.

usage.why_en: 眠る means to sleep; in the morning you get up (起きる), coffee keeps you awake, and rain falls (降る).

para.s: 【最近】、駅の近くに新しい店が多い。
para.why: このごろ means "these days".
para.en: Recently there are many new shops near the station.

wrong.3: 子供のころ means in childhood.

para.why_en: このごろ means 'these days'.

options: 最近、来週旅行に行きます。
最近、十年前に日本へ来ました。
usage.why: 最近 means the recent past up to now, not the future or long ago.
opts_en: Lately I haven't been sleeping well.
Recently, I'm going on a trip next week.
Recently, I came to Japan ten years ago.

1.why: Next week is the future; drop 最近.
1.fix: 来週、旅行に行きます。
1.fix_en: I'm going on a trip next week.

2.why: Ten years ago isn't recent; drop 最近.
2.fix: 十年前に日本へ来ました。
2.fix_en: I came to Japan ten years ago.

3.why: Tomorrow is the future; drop 最近.
3.fix: 明日は雨です。
3.fix_en: It will rain tomorrow.

usage.why_en: 最近 means the recent past up to now; it can't be used for the future or for long ago.

para.s: 山は【雪】で白くなった。
options: 冬に空から降る白いもの
para.why: 雪 is the white thing that falls in winter.
para.en: The mountain turned white with snow.
opts_en: white stuff that falls in winter
para.why_en: 雪 is the white thing that falls from the sky in winter.

options: 雪が強く吹いて、木がたおれた。
雪がたくさん降って、電車が止まった。
空で雪が鳴って、光った。
usage.why: Snow falls and is cold; wind blows and thunder (かみなり) rumbles.
opts_en: The snow blew hard and a tree fell over.
It snowed a lot, and the trains stopped.
My hands got hot from the snow.
Snow rumbled and flashed in the sky.

0.why: What blows (吹く) hard is wind (風).
